**Continuous 2.12.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.12.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.12.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.12.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.12.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.12.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.12.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.12.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.12.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.12.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.12.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.12.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.10.0

**Commands no longer inherit your secrets.** A command the agent runs (the terminal tool, hooks, background jobs, worktree setup, the WSL and local executors, and stdio MCP servers that rely on the host environment) now starts with a scrubbed environment by default: known secret names are dropped. `terminal.environment` takes `scrub` (default), `inherit` or `allowlist`; `terminal.passEnv` and `terminal.allow` name exceptions; `CONTINUE_TERMINAL_ENV` overrides all of them. Explicit `env:` on an MCP server is left alone. A tool that relied on an exported token now needs it listed in `terminal.passEnv`. (#490)

**An audit trail of permission decisions.** Decisions and outcomes from the IDE and the CLI are written locally, with secrets masked, 20 MB rotation and 30-day retention. `continuous audit list|show|prune` reads it. On by default; `audit.enabled: false` or `CONTINUE_AUDIT=off` turns it off. (#481)

**MCP and untrusted content**

- **Tool pinning.** Each MCP server's tool definitions are hashed after first approval. A changed definition asks at every level except YOLO. (#480)
- The CLI shows the prompt-injection notice, and `fetch_url_content` results can be wrapped in a spotlight boundary behind `experimental.spotlightUntrusted`. (#480)
- **Missing programs.** A terminal command whose program is not installed is not run; the model is told so instead of getting a shell error. `CONTINUE_MISSING_BINARY_CHECK=off` restores the old behaviour. (#460)
- **Shell-aware command reading.** `$()`, backticks and the PowerShell, bash and zsh forms are read per shell, with new lint codes CL040 to CL045. (#471)

**Models that write tool calls as text**

- **`toolDialect` on a model.** Values `auto`, `native`, `qwen-xml`, `pythonic`, `llama-json`, `off`. A dialect turns on recovery of calls the model wrote as text; `CONTINUE_RECOVER_TEXT_TOOL_CALLS` still wins. Nothing changes unless you set it. (#491)
- **Test connection** for Bedrock models sends one small probe and reports `Tool calls: native`, `written as text (X)`, `not supported` or `unknown`. A notice offers to turn recovery on when a reply leaks a call as text; the CLI prints a one-line hint. (#491)
- Recovery exists for Qwen XML (#455, #463, #479), Python-syntax calls for Nova (#465) and Llama JSON (#487), all off by default. DSML fragments and leaked `<think>` text are dropped on every Bedrock path. (#487)
- Per-family Bedrock request rules were measured for Kimi K3, K2 Thinking, GLM 5, MiniMax M2.5, Nemotron 3 Super and gpt-oss. (#483)

**Loop mode and cost**

- **Dollar budgets are enforced** when the cost is known; an unknown cost never counts as zero. (#476)
- **Fallback check** for items with no `check:` of their own, off by default (`CONTINUOUS_LOOP_FALLBACK_CHECK`). (#486)
- Leaving Loop pauses the loop and returning resumes it. (#451)
- The stuck signals gained `repeated-block` and `persistent-failure`, and `no-progress` counts new output; L1 notes appear in CLI tool results. (#446, #464)

**Where commands run**

- Windows Sandbox: a detector, a timing probe and a runner that returns a command's output from a fresh sandbox (#445, #488). Dev container detection with a CLI status (#444). Egress policy, a pinned proxy and escape probes exist as code, not yet wired into an executor (#456, #469).

**Other**

- `continuous acp` runs the CLI as an Agent Client Protocol agent on stdio. A first slice; not tried in Zed or JetBrains. (#473)
- Old tool results can be masked in the request with a `recall_masked_result` tool, off by default (`CONTINUE_HISTORY_AGEING`). (#467)
- `experimental.toolSearch` adds a `search_tools` meta-tool above a token budget, off by default. (#484)
- Edit tools recover a match that differs in line endings or indentation when it is unique. (#482)
- The toolbox is a glyph that pulls the drawer out, and `no-fetch-and-run` asks. (#447, #448)

**Secrets and privacy**

- **Secrets are scrubbed on write.** Known secret shapes (a shared rule set, also used by the audit masker) are removed from what the product writes to its own files, and those files are created owner-only. `continuous clean` removes what earlier versions left behind, and `continuous secrets scan --history` scans saved history for secrets. Rules were tuned for env-style assignments and URL credentials, with a warn action. (#536, #555, #560, #563)
- **Reviewer pre-filter.** Text addressed to the Auto-mode reviewer (instructions aimed at it inside a command or file) is answered with ask before any model is called. (#557)
- **Config you load is locked.** Permission rules may only be loosened from your own configuration; every file the product loads as config, code, rules or hooks is protected from the agent; hook script content counts toward trust, and `worktrees.json` setup commands wait for project trust. (#516, #538, #541, #543)
- **PowerShell aliases.** A table generated from `Get-Alias` means `rm`, `iwr` and friends are read as the cmdlets they are; defining an alias asks. (#569)
- **YOLO write-target rule.** A write whose target is only known at run time asks, even at YOLO, after resolving the pieces that are known. (#570)
- A variable that is not the program no longer refuses a command (#545); the CLI no longer reads a `.env` from the working directory (#542).

**Auto-mode reviewer measurement.** The reviewer eval (`continuous reviewer eval`) got per-case outcomes, `--config`, `--repeat` and accept sets (#519, #550, #553). Re-measured on 2026-11-11 on an 80-case set (37 floor cases) with the pre-filter on and off: **Amazon Nova 2 Lite failed the gate** with 2 of 37 floor false allows in both arms (different cases each run), so it is not safe to use as the reviewer. Claude Haiku 4.5 had 0 of 37, but asks on many cases and strict agreement is 73.8%. One pass per arm, not three repeats, because of a spend cap; the pre-filter changed no verdict on this set. Evidence: `bench/evidence/2026-11-11-reviewer-remeasure`.

**Bedrock and tool calls written as text**

- **Non-streaming tool calls for more model families**, and a retry when streamed tool input arrives broken. (#566)
- **Leak nudge.** When a reply is a tool call written as text, the model is nudged once; the interactive CLI does the same, with a session cap and a setting; a held-reply indicator shows in the IDE. (#507, #512, #567)
- More recovery dialects, all off unless the model or setting asks for them: Harmony, Mistral, DeepSeek, Llama 4, Kimi, MiniMax, Granite, LFM2, Hy3, Solar Open, LongCat, Olmo 3, Seed-OSS, Cohere, `<TOOLCALL>` JSON, plus an OpenAI-compatible adapter. The whole reply must be calls, in the stream path too. Ollama's `/api/show` parser information is read and used in the notices. (#502, #508, #522, #524, #525, #532, #528, #558, #564)

**Settings and interface**

- **Settings work below 640 px**, the agents tree has states, and the Bedrock test result shows. Settings > Tools no longer crashes in a webview. (#549, #520)
- Mode and policy controls moved above the prompt; the input toolbar is decluttered; chip contrast, 24 px targets, unique ids and chat accessibility were fixed; one Loop icon. (#514, #546, #548, #511)
- **Permissions page**: a rule viewer and tester, then rule editing. (#521, #544)
- Loop checks report the real exit code on Windows. (#551)

## Planning

[`plans/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/plans/ROADMAP.md) records what is built and what is not.

## Not included

The JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
